quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When following another vehicle at night, use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when you are within 300 feet of another vehicle. High beams can blind the other driver and reduce their visibility.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off the moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is ahead.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead with no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down while passing the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your path, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk. Always stop and let them cross safely.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you begin driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seat belt, and secure any loose items. Never adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
Will always stop at the upcoming railroad crossing.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: The MVA will suspend your license if you:

options.text: Refuse to use a false ID to buy alcohol.
Fail to meet school attendance requirements.
Refuse to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test.
questions.explanation: If you refuse a BAC test, the MVA will suspend your license based on a police report of the refusal.

questions.question: The maximum speed limit should only be driven:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum safe speed only when conditions are perfect. Always drive at a safe speed for the current weather and traffic.

questions.question: An important step when turning is to:

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind you and to both sides to make sure it is safe. Slow down to make the turn safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. It is unsafe and illegal to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection if it is safe and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection if it is safe and clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you may proceed. First, check that the intersection is clear of other cars and pedestrians. Yield to anyone already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt your reaction time, coordination, alertness, and ability to focus. All of these skills are needed for safe driving.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and keep going at the same speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.

questions.explanation: If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down. Be ready to stop if they step into your path.

questions.question: Which of these is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass where you cannot see far ahead, such as on hills or curves. Never pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, or where no passing signs are posted. Do not pass with a solid yellow line next to your lane.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reactions, makes it hard to judge speed and distance, and causes poor decisions. You could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, hurting yourself or others.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead, such as a change in road direction, a steep downgrade, or other dangerous conditions.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, how can you reduce the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. A cold shower, exercise, or coffee will not speed up this process. It takes about one hour per drink.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: It is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means it is illegal and unsafe to pass in that area. You likely cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes, with or without a red tip.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription drugs and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you do not think about it.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to calm down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how safely you drive. If you are angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, take time to calm down before driving. You need to focus your mind on driving safely.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when can you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, check your rearview mirror until you see both headlights of the passed vehicle. Only then is it safe to return to your original lane.

questions.question: Is texting while driving legal?

options.text: Yes, if you are driving slowly.
Yes, if you are 21 or older.

questions.explanation: Maryland law does not allow drivers to use handheld cell phones while driving. Hands-free devices are allowed, but drivers should limit calls and focus on safe driving. Using a cell phone while driving is distracted driving and increases accident risk.
